name: Nest Doorbell wired 2nd gen (US)

radios.note: Google's install page requires a Wi-Fi network with at least 2 Mbps upload. The Google spec page for the original wired model lists 2.4 GHz 802.11b/g/n; the retailer listings seen say dual band, so the bands are not confirmed for this model.

matter.note: No Matter claim found in the Google pages checked; the CSA database was not searched.

apple_home.note: No Google or Apple page found that lists this doorbell in Apple Home.

google_home.note: Set up in the Google Home app. Doorbell visitor announcements play on Google speakers and displays in the same home; familiar-face names need a paid Google plan.

alexa.note: Linked through Alexa and the Google Home app. Doorbell-press announcements work on this model once Visitor announcements is on in Google Home. Live view works on Echo Show after you ask for it: wired models stream for up to 12 hours before you must ask again.

home_assistant.note: The official Google Nest integration lists the wired 2nd gen doorbell with WebRTC live view and motion, person and chime events. It runs on Google's Device Access API, which has a one-time US$5 fee.

hubRequired.note: Needs Wi-Fi, the Google Home app and a Google Account; no hub or bridge is mentioned.

localControl.note: Google does not state whether any control works without its cloud.

power.note: Needs existing doorbell wiring; some homes need a stronger transformer. It has no battery and cannot use the chime connector from the 1st gen.

localStorage.note: Google says it can hold up to an hour of events in the doorbell if Wi-Fi drops, but no local or microSD storage option is stated.

subscription.note: Google lists 3 hours of event video with no plan; Nest Aware adds 30 days of event history and familiar-face alerts, and Nest Aware Plus adds continuous recording.

summary: Nest Doorbell (wired, 2nd gen) is a Wi-Fi video doorbell that runs on existing 16 to 24 V AC doorbell wiring. It works natively with Google Home and also with Alexa, which announces doorbell presses and can show live view on Echo Show. Home Assistant supports it through the Google Nest integration. Without a plan it keeps 3 hours of event video.
caveats: Needs doorbell wiring and a transformer that meets the 16–24 V AC requirement; it has no battery.
Video history beyond 3 hours needs a paid Nest Aware plan.
Home Assistant access goes through Google's Device Access API, which has a one-time US$5 fee.
Apple Home support is not confirmed.
